summary: Park Ridge in Kings Canyon National Park has been a fire lookout site since 1916, is reached only on foot, and is staffed by volunteers.

facts.design: Steel tower about 20 feet high, with a cab on top

access.note: Open daily to the public during fire season, usually mid-May through October; may close without notice.

visit.trail_note: Hike 5 miles round trip from Panoramic Point, or take the 5-mile loop from the Manzanita Trail. No water or toilet on site.

events.note: Established as an open-air platform with a lean-to shelter.
Two-story wooden lookout, per the register. The NPS article dates it to 1934.
Park Service took sole responsibility; joint management with the Forest Service ended.
Mattie Simms staffed it every fire season from June 1956.
Steel tower replaced the wooden lookout and was moved about a quarter mile southwest.
Register says its 13-foot-square CL-100 cab went into service.
Mattie Simms retired in October 1974; staffing was sporadic afterward.
Reopened under a cooperative agreement; Buck Rock Foundation volunteers staff it each fire season.
Ceremony at the lookout marking the register listing, August 3, 2013.

evidence.supports: Location: southern end of Park Ridge, east of Grant Grove, Kings Canyon NP
evidence.quote: Park Ridge Lookout is located on the southern end of Park Ridge just east of Grant Grove, in Kings Canyon National Park

evidence.supports: Site first used for fire detection in 1916
evidence.quote: The site of Park Ridge Lookout on the Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Park was first used for fire detection in 1916.

evidence.supports: Original open-air lookout with lean-to shelter
evidence.quote: Park Ridge was originally an open air lookout with a lean-to shelter and a tent platform.

evidence.supports: Established 1916 as open-air platform with lean-to
evidence.quote: Park Ridge Lookout was established in 1916 as an open-air platform with a lean-to shelter.

evidence.supports: Two-story wooden lookout dated 1929 by register
evidence.quote: In 1929 a two story live-in wooden lookout was constructed by the USFS and UPS.

evidence.supports: NPS dates two-story wooden lookout to 1934; steel tower replaced it in 1964
evidence.quote: In 1934 a classic two-story wooden lookout was built, but it was replaced in 1964 by a 20-foot high, 14-by-14 foot steel tower, which remains in place today.

evidence.supports: Joint USFS and NPS management ended 1940 with sole NPS responsibility
evidence.quote: The lookout was jointly managed by the National Park Service and U.S. Forest Service until 1940 when the Park Service assumed sole responsibility for the lookout.

evidence.supports: 1964 wooden lookout replaced by current steel tower
evidence.quote: In 1964, the original wooden lookout, with lower living quarters, was replaced by the current 20 foot high

evidence.supports: Tower moved about a quarter mile southwest of original site
evidence.quote: was moved ¼ mile SW of the original site

evidence.supports: Register: 13x13 ft CL-100 cab on 20 ft tower went into service 1967
evidence.quote: this 13'x13' CL-100 cab on a 20' tower went into service in 1967.

evidence.supports: Mattie Simms staffed every fire season June 1956 to retirement October 1974
evidence.quote: Park Ridge was staffed every fire season by Mattie Simms from June 1956 until her retirement in October 1974.

evidence.supports: NPS article spells the firewatcher's name Sims
evidence.quote: Kay Coffin, daughter of long-time Park Ridge fire watcher Mattie Sims

evidence.supports: Staffing sporadic after 1974; closed permanently 1996
evidence.quote: After Mattie retired, the lookout was staffed only sporadically for many years and was closed permanently in 1996.

evidence.supports: Buck Rock Foundation led the nomination to the register
evidence.quote: Buck Rock Foundation took the lead in collaboration with Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks in nominating Park Ridge Lookout for the National Historic Lookout Register.

evidence.supports: Date registered October 19, 2010
evidence.quote: October 19, 2010

evidence.supports: Ceremony on August 3, 2013 to honor the register listing
evidence.quote: On Saturday, August 3, 2013, thirty people gathered at a ceremony at Park Ridge Lookout in Kings Canyon National Park to honor the recent addition of the lookout to the National Historic Lookout Register.

evidence.supports: Reopened 2004 under cooperative agreement; volunteers staff each fire season
evidence.quote: Through a cooperative agreement between the Buck Rock Foundation and the National Park Service, Park Ridge reopened in 2004 and continues to be staffed every fire season by Buck Rock Foundation volunteer firewatchers.

evidence.supports: Open daily to the public 10:30 am to 5 pm in fire season, usually mid-May to October
evidence.quote: Park Ridge Lookout is open daily to the public from 10:30 am to 5:00 pm during fire season, which is usually mid-May through October

evidence.supports: Hike of 5 miles round trip from Panoramic Point or 5-mile loop from Manzanita Trail
evidence.quote: Get to Park Ridge by hiking the trail from Panoramic Point (5 miles round-trip) or from the Manzanita Trail (5 mile loop).

evidence.supports: No vehicle access
evidence.quote: There is no vehicle access.

evidence.supports: No water or toilet on site; trash must be packed out
evidence.quote: There is no public toilet or water available on site, and no garbage service

evidence.supports: Normally staffed around the clock
evidence.quote: Park Ridge Lookout is normally staffed 24 hours-a-day, 7 days-a-week.

evidence.supports: Cab is workplace and residence for the firewatcher
evidence.quote: The lookout is used as both work place and residence for the firewatcher on duty.

evidence.supports: Open for the 2026 fire season
evidence.quote: PARK RIDGE LOOKOUT is OPEN for the 2026 fire season.

evidence.supports: May close without notice for fire activity or weather
evidence.quote: may be closed at any time without notice due to fire activity

evidence.supports: Visitors asked to pack out trash
evidence.quote: please pack out your trash

evidence.supports: Steel tower 14 by 14 feet, per Buck Rock
evidence.quote: 14’ X 14’ steel tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1964 steel tower replaced the wooden lookout according to Buck Rock and the NPS article. The register gives 1964 as the build year and says the cab went into service in 1967.

sources.title: Wildland Fire: Park Ridge Lookout National Historic Lookout Register

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the two-story wooden lookout is dated 1929 by the register and 1934 by the NPS article. The cab is 13 by 13 feet per the register, while Buck Rock and the NPS give the steel tower as 14 by 14 feet. The firewatcher's surname is spelled Simms by Buck Rock and Sims by the NPS. Elevation is 7,471 ft in the register and 7,520 ft on Buck Rock. Current hours come from a 2026 Buck Rock page and should be rechecked before publication. The French Wikipedia stub was read but not used.
